podcast.body: The first single from "The Soul Cages," this was a jaunty pop song and one of Sting's friendliest hits, featuring a lead melody line played by a mandolin. It reached number five on the Hot 100 in March 1991 and number one on the modern rock chart. A close listen to the lyrics reveals it is about Sting's deceased father, describing a funeral and imagining a burial at sea, culminating in the question, "Father, if Jesus exists, then how come he never lived here?" "However, a close listen to the lyrics revealed that the song was actually about Sting's deceased father who had passed since his previous album."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
